subject: computer-science
source_note: Topic structure follows the reformed IB Diploma Computer Science guide (first teaching 2025, first exams 2027), Themes A and B with HL extension content. Topic names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

units.name: A1 — Computer Fundamentals
units.blurb: Hardware, data, operating systems and translation

units.name: A3 — Databases

units.name: A4 — Machine Learning
units.blurb: Machine learning approaches, data and ethics

units.name: B4 — Abstract Data Types (HL)
units.blurb: Linked lists, trees, sets and hash tables (HL only)

connections.why: Data representation underlies how hardware stores and processes data

Machine learning depends on suitable processing hardware
Operating systems manage the network connections of a device
Translators turn the source code programmers write into machine code
Network fundamentals frame how architectures are built
Network architecture shapes how data is transmitted
Data transmission introduces the vulnerabilities security must address
Client-server architecture hosts shared databases
Database fundamentals guide sound database design
A well-designed schema is queried through database programming
Relational limits motivate alternative databases and warehouses
Data warehouses supply the large datasets machine learning needs
Stored data is the raw material machine learning trains on
Raw data must be preprocessed before models can learn from it
Preprocessed features feed the machine learning algorithms
Powerful ML approaches sharpen the ethical questions they raise
Understanding ML raises the ethical questions it must address
Computational thinking is expressed through programming constructs
Algorithm design is a core part of computational thinking
Fundamentals are combined into selection and iteration constructs
Data structures determine the efficiency of algorithms
Procedural constructs are encapsulated within classes
Object-oriented programming builds on programming fundamentals
A single class extends to inheritance across multiple classes
Built-in data structures generalise to abstract data types
Trees and hash tables enable efficient search algorithms
Classes are used to implement abstract data types
Search algorithms parallel how databases retrieve records
File processing is the simpler precursor to database storage
Abstraction and pattern recognition underpin machine learning
